themes_detail.label: Park Disruption Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park-related complaints—including noise and rule violations—spiked dramatically THIS WEEK, with 6 noise complaints (vs. 0.8 weekly average) and 4 rule violations (vs. 0.2 weekly average), a 700% and 1500% increase respectively, suggesting a sudden shift in park usage or enforcement patterns.
evidence: Noise - Park complaints: 6 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.94, +700%)
Violation of Park Rules complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.67, +1500%)
Litter Basket Requests: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.5, +900%), suggesting park sanitation strain
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about what changed in Jackson Heights parks this week—new events, closures, or enforcement shifts
Canvass park regulars and nearby residents about disruptions, noise sources, and rule-breaking patterns
Investigate whether understaffing or lack of maintenance (per recurring CB budget requests for 'park maintenance and safety') is contributing to chaos

themes_detail.label: Encampment Spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints doubled over the past 2 weeks, reaching 8 complaints 2 weeks ago versus 1.8 weekly average—a 357% spike (z-score: 3.05)—indicating a potential homelessness or street conditions deterioration.
evidence: Encampment complaints: 8 (2 weeks ago) vs. 1.8 weekly baseline (+357%, z-score: 3.05)
Concurrent spike in Commercial Disposal complaints (4 vs. 1.1 avg, +256%), suggesting waste/sanitation strain
Curb Condition complaints elevated last week (4 vs. 1.1 avg, +256%), indicating street degradation
reporting_angles: Map where encampments have appeared; interview affected residents and local businesses
Contact NYC Department of Social Services and outreach teams to understand why Jackson Heights/Corona is seeing increased visibility
Investigate whether budget constraints (per CB's recurring 'street reconstruction' and 'park maintenance' requests) have reduced cleaning and enforcement capacity

themes_detail.label: Skateboarding/Wheeled Activity Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about biking, skating, and roller activities surged to 3 complaints 2 weeks ago from a 0.1 weekly baseline—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting either new youth activity, a safety incident, or enforcement action in the district.
evidence: Bike/Roller/Skate complaints: 3 (2 weeks ago) vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (+2300%, z-score: 8.69)
This is the largest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating a rare concentrated event
No supporting Reddit or news coverage yet, suggesting this may be under-reported locally
reporting_angles: Identify the location(s) where skateboarding/biking complaints clustered—likely a specific park, plaza, or street
Interview NYPD precinct or Parks Enforcement about what triggered the spike (new park policy, event, or crackdown)
Talk to youth in the area about wheeled sports culture and whether a new spot has become popular

themes_detail.label: Trash & Curb Maintenance Decline
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests hit 5 complaints THIS WEEK (vs. 0.5 baseline, +900%) while curb condition complaints remained elevated last week at 4 (vs. 1.1 baseline, +256%), suggesting deteriorating street sanitation and possible reduction in maintenance service frequency.
evidence: Litter Basket Requests: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (+900%, z-score: 4.5)
Curb Condition complaints: 4 (last week) vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (+256%, z-score: 2.73)
Long-running CB budget request for 'street reconstruction' and 'DEP capital' suggests chronic under-resourcing
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation about service schedules and staffing levels in CD 403 this week
Walk streets to document trash accumulation and missing/full litter baskets
Review Community Board minutes to see if maintenance cuts or service reductions were discussed
